key_insight: AegisDx reframes AI diagnosis as a safety-first reasoning workflow that broadens differentials, checks for “must-not-miss” conditions, and verifies outputs against evidence rather than making a single prediction.
clinical_relevance: For acute care support, this could reduce missed high-risk diagnoses and make AI-assisted differential diagnosis more transparent and clinically usable.
method: Coordinates multiple LLM roles with explicit contracts
Uses structured intermediate outputs and evidence-retrieval/verification gates
Forces screening for dangerous “must-not-miss” diagnoses and actionable next steps
evidence_signal: Across case-report and emergency-department evaluations, AegisDx outperformed a standalone LLM on Top-3 diagnostic accuracy and improved physician-rated safety scores, including better capture of must-not-miss conditions.
watch_item: Results are promising but come from retrospective and blinded evaluation settings, so real-world workflow impact, calibration, and safety under deployment still need prospective validation.
paper_title: A safety-oriented hypothetico-deductive framework for AI-assisted differential diagnosis
